question: Ticket 150133a3ca74 says 'When the cast door refuses, run_proof catches RedTicketRefused and raises an unticketed trouble, re-raising so the run still exits non-zero. The red stays in the new-red category for the next run.', but outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 reads "Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead." (The outline states: 'Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds...'. After this ticket is built, when the door refuses, no ticket is written—only an unticketed trouble is recorded. This violates the outline's requirement that each run successfully tickets new reds. The outline does not contemplate or allow for the case where the ticket door fails; the clause 'unless one is already open for it' refers only to pre-existing tickets, not to failures of the ticketing mechanism itself.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The outline stands. The door already refuses today and leaves nothing on disk (measured on akiendell 2026-11-23: three sorted berths, no ticket, no trace). The ticket adds no exception; it makes the unmet 9.4.2.3.7.5 visible as a trouble that clears only when the red is ticketed. Added as a constraint.
